```text
# TASK-0128: Stop the FormatSelector active button dimming on hover

In `FormatSelector/FormatSelector.tsx`, `btnBase` includes `text-text-muted hover:text-text-secondary`, and `btnActive` adds `text-text-primary`. Two problems follow:

- **It dims on hover.** The active button still has the base `hover:text-text-secondary`, so hovering it drops the text from 98% to 85% lightness.
- **The active color is fragile.** `text-text-primary` only wins over `text-text-muted` because Tailwind happens to emit `.text-text-primary` later in the CSS. Change the order and the active button silently turns muted.

## Fix

Keep the color classes separate from the shared base:

- the shared base has no text color;
- the inactive state gets `text-text-muted hover:text-text-secondary`;
- the active state gets `text-text-primary`.

Another option is `cn()` (tailwind-merge), if the project adopts it.

## Acceptance

- The active button stays `text-primary` when hovered.
- The active and inactive color classes never appear on the same element.

## Source

- Review of commit 3e17daa (2026-10-30): a11y reviewer.

# TASK-0120: Rename saturation mode labels

The saturation slider's mode toggle shows the raw `satMode` value, `endpoint` or `target`, as its visible label. Neither reads as a curve parameter. Since the target color input (TASK-0046) shipped, "target" also means two different things in the same control bar: the L50 saturation mode, and the user-entered target color.

## Candidate labels (from NOTE-0012)

- **edges / center** — describes where the slider acts on the curve
- **ends / vertex** — more mathematical, but precise
- **range / peak** — describes the saturation behavior

## Scope

- Choose the new pair and update the visible label in `SaturationSlider/SaturationSlider.tsx`. It currently renders `{satMode}` directly, so the display string needs to decouple from the enum value.
- Decide whether to also rename the internal `"endpoint" | "target"` union (used by `paletteStore` and `getSaturation()` in `lib/palette.ts`) or keep it as an internal identifier with a display-label map.
- Update any About dialog, chart, or export copy that refers to the modes by name.

## Acceptance

- The visible mode labels no longer use "target", and nothing collides with the target color feature.
- The toggle's accessible name and tooltip/title copy match the new labels.
- No behavior change to the curve math.

## Related

- TASK-0119 — Add hover tooltips to control labels (tooltip copy should use the new labels).
- TASK-0084 — Disambiguate "fixed saturation" labels in About dialog (adjacent copy work).

# TASK-0084: Disambiguate "fixed saturation" labels in About dialog

In the About dialog's opening explanation, the comparison strips are labeled **"Fixed low saturation"** and **"Fixed high saturation"** to mean *constant* saturation — i.e., the saturation value doesn't vary with lightness. But the surrounding narrative is all about *fixing* (correcting) a perceptual problem, so "fixed" reads ambiguously as "corrected" — the opposite of what's meant.

## Fix

Replace "Fixed" with an unambiguous synonym for "constant/uniform." Candidates:

- **"Static low saturation" / "Static high saturation"** — clearest match for "doesn't vary."
- **"Linear low saturation" / "Linear high saturation"** — accurate (saturation is constant across the lightness axis), and frames the comparison as linear-vs-curve, which is technically precise.
- **"Constant low saturation"** — clearest in plain English but a long word.
- **"Uniform"** — also accurate, similar trade-off.

"Linear" is probably the strongest because it implicitly contrasts with "curve" — the tool's whole identity. "Static" is the safest plain-English option.

## Acceptance

- Strip labels in `About.tsx` no longer use the word "fixed."
- Surrounding narrative copy is updated for consistency if needed.
- The opening paragraphs make clear that the comparison is **constant saturation vs. saturation that varies with lightness via the curve**.

## Related

- EPIC-0016 (parent).
- See [About.tsx](app/src/components/About.tsx) and any associated copy file.

# TASK-0078: Lock range slider by default

The lightness range slider should be **locked by default** so the two thumbs move together and preserve the symmetric range as a single value. Users who want asymmetric endpoints can unlock it explicitly.

## Why

Most users want a balanced palette around the midpoint; the symmetric range is the dominant use case. Defaulting unlocked means the first interaction often produces a lopsided range unintentionally, which feels like noise rather than a feature.

## Acceptance

- New sessions start with the range slider locked.
- Lock state continues to persist (existing behavior — verify it still saves to the store).
- Verify the locked default produces an intuitive first-drag experience: dragging either thumb mirrors the other.

## Related

- TASK-0056 (deferred) — lock toggle on hue/saturation sliders. Same lock primitive; check that defaults align across all three.

# TASK-0126: Stop layout shift when copying a value in TargetFormats

Clicking a value in the TARGET formats row (`TargetFormats/TargetFormats.tsx`) replaces it with "Copied". The button shrinks, and every value after it slides left. At 1280px, the RGB button goes from 144px to 77px, and HSL and OKLCH move 67px left. This predates this task.

The values also change length while you drag Hue or Saturation, so the row jitters during a drag.

## Fix options

- Stack "Copied" over the value in a single grid cell (`grid` with both children in `[grid-area:1/1]`) and make the value `invisible` while "Copied" shows. The button then keeps the value's width.
- Fixed-width value cells, sized to the longest string for each format.

## Acceptance

- Copying a value doesn't move any other element in the row.
- Dragging the sliders doesn't reflow the row at lg widths.

## Related

- TASK-0102: Redesign the swatch copy-feedback overlay (the same problem on palette swatches).
- TASK-0121: A mono typeface for color values would fix some of the width jitter.
```

```text
# EPIC-0017: Control defaults and affordances

The curve-shaping controls (hue, saturation, adjustment, lightness range) ship with defaults that don't match the canonical perception-corrected curve, and they offer no clean path back to defaults once the user has tweaked. This makes the *first impression* weaker than it should be (defaults that produce pure black/white endpoints, an unlocked range that drifts asymmetric on the first drag) and the *recovery path* nonexistent (no reset).

## Goals

- First-load state should reflect the canonical perception-corrected curve — the published default — so a user who opens the app and changes nothing already sees the tool's thesis.
- Defaults should bias toward the dominant use case (symmetric range, fully chromatic endpoints), with explicit affordances for the asymmetric/edge cases.
- Reset paths exist, are visible only when the control has been modified, and communicate that the default *is* the canonical curve.

## Tasks

- TASK-0078 — Lock range slider by default
- TASK-0079 — Rework lightness range defaults and endpoint handling
```

```text
import chroma from "chroma-js";
import type { ColorEntry, PaletteParams, SatMode } from "../types/palette";

/**
 * Parabolic saturation curve centered at lightness 50%.
 * See: https://www.desmos.com/calculator/02ufrfsuzy
 *
 * In "endpoint" mode the multiplier is 1.0 at L0/L100 (slider = endpoint saturation).
 * In "target" mode the multiplier is 1.0 at L50 (slider = vertex/target saturation).
 */
export function getSaturation(
  lightness: number,
  sMod: number,
  satMode: SatMode,
): number {
  if (sMod === 0) return 1;
  const o = 50;
  const raw =
    1 + (Math.pow(lightness - o, 2) / sMod - Math.pow(o, 2) / sMod) / 100;

  if (satMode === "endpoint") return raw;

  // Normalize so vertex (L50) = 1.0, endpoints > 1.0
  const vertex = 1 - Math.pow(o, 2) / sMod / 100;
  if (vertex <= 0) return raw;
  return raw / vertex;
}

export function generateNeutrals(params: PaletteParams): ColorEntry[] {
  const { hue, saturation, sMod, satMode, lMin, lMax } = params;

  const entries: ColorEntry[] = [];

  for (let i = lMin; i <= lMax; i++) {
    const l = i / 100;
    const sK = getSaturation(i, sMod, satMode);
    const color = chroma.hsl(hue, saturation * sK, l);

    const [h, s, lVal] = color.hsl();
    const hRound = Math.round(h) || 0;
    const sRound = Math.round(s * 10000) / 100;
    const lRound = Math.round(lVal * 10000) / 100;

    entries.push({
      label: `grey-${i}`,
      lightness: i,
      hsl: [h, s, lVal],
      hslString: `${hRound} ${sRound}% ${lRound}%`,
      hex: color.hex(),
    });
  }

  return entries.reverse();
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-04 23:01:31Z)**_

As colors, yes. In this app, no: the palette only has entries at whole-number L values.

- `app/src/lib/palette.ts:34` builds one entry per integer L (`i++`), and the range slider uses `step={1}` (`app/src/components/LightnessRange/LightnessRange.tsx:73`).
- `sampleEntries` (`app/src/components/PaletteGrid/PaletteGrid.tsx:33`) can only pick from those entries. That's why 12.5 rounds to 13.
- The math itself accepts fractions. `getSaturation()` is a continuous parabola, `chroma.hsl()` takes any `l` from 0 to 1, and CSS `hsl(… 12.5%)` is valid.

Fractional L does break names. The label `grey-${i}` (`app/src/lib/palette.ts:45`) would become `grey-12.5`:
- **CSS export** (`app/src/lib/export.ts:59`): `--grey-12.5` is invalid because `.` isn't allowed in a CSS name. In a test with lightningcss the declaration was dropped. It would have to be written `--grey-12\.5`.
- **SCSS** (`app/src/lib/export.ts:93`): `$grey-12.5` hits the same rule, so it's a syntax error. I didn't run this one because Sass isn't installed.
- **Tailwind v4** (`app/src/lib/export.ts:66`): fine. Tailwind 4.2.1 escapes the dot itself, and `bg-grey-12.5` worked when I tested it.
- **tw3 / JS / JSON**: fine. Their keys come from `String(e.lightness)`, giving `"12.5"`.

So exact 12.5 steps would need two changes: generate colors at fractional L, and name swatches by something other than the raw L value. TASK-0087 (label and count semantics) is where that naming decision belongs.

```text
import chroma from "chroma-js";
import type { ColorEntry, ExportFormat, ColorSpace } from "../types/palette";

function colorValue(entry: ColorEntry, space: ColorSpace): string {
  const c = chroma(entry.hex);
  switch (space) {
    case "hsl":
      return `hsl(${entry.hslString})`;
    case "hex":
      return entry.hex;
    case "rgb": {
      const [r, g, b] = c.rgb();
      return `rgb(${r}, ${g}, ${b})`;
    }
    case "hcl": {
      const [h, c2, l] = c.hcl();
      const hR = Math.round(h || 0);
      const cR = Math.round((c2 || 0) * 10) / 10;
      const lR = Math.round(l * 10) / 10;
      return `hcl(${hR}, ${cR}, ${lR})`;
    }
    case "oklch": {
      const [l, c2, h] = c.oklch();
      const lR = Math.round(l * 1000) / 1000;
      const cR = Math.round((c2 || 0) * 1000) / 1000;
      const hR = Math.round(h || 0);
      return `oklch(${lR} ${cR} ${hR})`;
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Format a color at hue/sat/L=50 in the given format.
 */
export function formatTargetColor(
  hue: number,
  saturation: number,
  format: ColorFormat,
): string {
  const color = chroma.hsl(hue, saturation, 0.5);
  switch (format) {
    case "hsl":
      return `hsl(${hue}, ${Math.round(saturation * 100)}%, 50%)`;
    case "rgb": {
      const [r, g, b] = color.rgb();
      return `rgb(${Math.round(r)}, ${Math.round(g)}, ${Math.round(b)})`;
    }
    case "oklch":
      return toOklchString(color.hex());
    default:
      return color.hex();
  }
}

export function toOklchString(hex: string): string {
  const [l, c, h] = chroma(hex).oklch();
  const lR = Math.round(l * 1000) / 1000;
  const cR = Math.round((c || 0) * 1000) / 1000;
  const hR = Math.round(h || 0);
  return `oklch(${lR} ${cR} ${hR})`;
}

export interface AllFormats {
  hex: string;
  rgb: string;
  hsl: string;
  oklch: string;
}

/**
 * Return all four string representations of a color at hue/sat/L=50.
 */
export function formatAllFormats(hue: number, saturation: number): AllFormats {
  return {
    hex: formatTargetColor(hue, saturation, "hex"),
    rgb: formatTargetColor(hue, saturation, "rgb"),
    hsl: formatTargetColor(hue, saturation, "hsl"),
    oklch: formatTargetColor(hue, saturation, "oklch"),
  };
}
```

```text
# TASK-0087: Decide label and count semantics for named scales

Planning task that locks down cross-feature decisions blocking implementation of named scales (Tailwind preset, B/W bookends, custom intervals, named colors).

## Decisions

- **Label model**: optional `label` field on each `ColorEntry`. String only, or structured (kind, value)?
- **Count semantics when features compose**: count = 8 with B/W on → 8 or 10? Tailwind preset (11) + B/W → 13 or override? Custom intervals — labels follow positions?
- **Default labeling**: with no preset active, show numeric labels or stay unlabeled?
- **Export labels**: bookends export as `white`/`black`; Tailwind exports as `gray-50` etc.; custom intervals — by index or position?

## Acceptance

- Decision recorded in this task body or a follow-up NOTE.
- Label data model specified for `ColorEntry`.
- Count semantics specified for: bare, +B/W, +Tailwind, +B/W+Tailwind, +custom intervals.

# TASK-0088: Rework ColorEntry label generation per decided semantics

Implement the label data model decided in TASK-0087 on top of the existing `ColorEntry.label` field, and make sure every consumer handles the new shape.

> **Refreshed 2026-10-20.** The original title ("Add `label` field to ColorEntry") assumed the field didn't exist. It does, and has since the React rebuild (3bfeef6): `ColorEntry.label: string` is hard-coded in `lib/palette.ts` as `` `grey-${i}` `` — a leftover from the "Chroma Neutrals" naming. It already flows into swatch rendering (`ColorSwatch` title + visible label) and into every export format as the token name (`--grey-N`, `--color-grey-N`, `$grey-N`, GPL/plain-text names). The work is changing how labels are *generated* and what shape they take, not adding the field.

## Acceptance

- `ColorEntry.label` matches the shape decided in TASK-0087 (e.g. required step label plus an optional human-readable name, if that's the decision).
- `generateNeutrals()` (or its OKLCH replacement) stops hard-coding `grey-${i}` and populates labels from the active preset/feature (step numbers, Tailwind shade names, B/W bookends).
- ColorSwatch renders any new optional label parts when present and gracefully omits them when absent.
- Export token names stay valid CSS custom-property / SCSS identifiers for every label scheme.
```

```text
      title={`${entry.label} - click to copy ${copyFormat.toUpperCase()}`}
    >
      {showLabels && (
        <>
          <span className="mb-4 origin-left text-sm font-semibold transition-transform group-hover:scale-105">
            {entry.label}
          </span>
          <span className="text-sm">{entry.hex}</span>
          <span className="text-2xs">hsl({entry.hslString})</span>
          <span className="text-2xs">{oklch}</span>
        </>
      )}
      <CopyFeedback visible={isCopied} />
    </button>
  );
}
```

Swatches now support one-decimal L values. With the default range, 9 swatches are exactly 0, 12.5, 25, 37.5, 50, 62.5, 75, 87.5 and 100. Saturation is now symmetric around L50 (42.19% at both 12.5 and 87.5).

The changes are on `feat/default-nine-swatches` and not committed yet:
- **`app/src/lib/palette.ts`**: `generateNeutrals(params, count?)` takes an optional count. With a count, it makes that many evenly spaced swatches at their exact L, rounded to 0.1. Without one, or if the count is at least the number of whole-number steps, it returns the one-per-integer list as before.
- **`app/src/hooks/usePalette.ts`**: passes the optional `count` through.
- **`app/src/components/PaletteGrid/PaletteGrid.tsx`**: now calls `usePalette(swatchCount)`. I deleted `sampleEntries`.
- **`app/src/lib/palette.test.ts`** (new): checks the exact 12.5 steps for 9 swatches, 0.1 rounding for 8 (14.3, 28.6 …), and the fallback to whole numbers.

The charts, the gradient strip, export and "all (101)" still use whole-number L, so export names never contain a dot like `grey-12.5`.

Correction to my earlier message: before this change, 9 swatches landed on L12, 37, 62 and 87, not 13, 38, 63 and 88.

Typecheck, knip, tests (6/6) and build pass. Lint still shows the same 26 warnings, none new. In the browser at 1280px the labels fit, with no console errors; the screenshot is at `.screenshots/nine-swatches-fractional-l.png`. I left the dev server running on `localhost:8200`.

Saturation input still works in whole percents. `parseTargetColor` (`app/src/lib/colors.ts:36`) rounds to 1%, so a target of `hsl(220 41.8% 50%)` becomes 42%, and the slider moves in 1% steps.

Should saturation keep one decimal too? I'd change the target-color parsing and the saturation readouts, and leave the slider and arrow-key steps at 1%, since 0.1% steps would make keyboard use 10× slower. import chroma from "chroma-js";

```text
const WCAG_AA_CONTRAST = 4.5;

export function getContrastColor(bgColor: string): string {
  const whiteContrast = chroma.contrast("white", bgColor);
  return whiteContrast < WCAG_AA_CONTRAST ? "#1d1d1d" : "#ffffff";
}

export type ColorFormat = "hex" | "hsl" | "rgb" | "oklch" | "named";

/**
 * Parse a color string and extract hue (0-360), saturation (0-1), and input format.
 * Supports hex, rgb(), hsl(), oklch() (incl. "/ alpha", which is ignored), and
 * named CSS colors.
 */
export function parseTargetColor(
  input: string,
): { hue: number; saturation: number; format: ColorFormat } | null {
  const trimmed = input.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return null;

  try {
    // Detect format before parsing
    const lower = trimmed.toLowerCase();
    let format: ColorFormat = "named";
    if (lower.startsWith("#")) format = "hex";
    else if (lower.startsWith("hsl")) format = "hsl";
    else if (lower.startsWith("rgb")) format = "rgb";
    else if (lower.startsWith("oklch")) format = "oklch";

    // chroma's CSS parser is case-sensitive for function names
    const [hue, sat] = chroma(lower).hsl();
    return {
      hue: Math.round(isNaN(hue) ? 0 : hue),
      saturation: Math.round((isNaN(sat) ? 0 : sat) * 100) / 100,
      format,
    };
  } catch {
    return null;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-04 23:53:23Z)**_

Saturation and lightness now keep one decimal everywhere. I held off on the rounding setting because one decimal is already finer than a hex color can show. A 0.1% step in S or L moves an RGB channel by at most about half an 8-bit step, so extra decimals would change nothing you can see. A setting would only help for whole-number output, for tools that reject decimals. The precision is defined in one function, `roundPercent()` in `app/src/lib/colors.ts`, so adding a setting later is a small change. The export dialog would be the natural place for it.

**What changed**
- **One source of truth:** everything that rounds S or L now calls `roundPercent()`. That covers swatch L steps, the swatch HSL text, target-color parsing, the target's HSL value, and the slider and picker readouts.
- **Typed `hsl()` targets:** saturation is now read straight from the text. chroma.js converts `hsl()` to 8-bit RGB first, which is why `hsl(220 41.8% 50%)` used to become 42% and `hsl(220 41.8% 10%)` became 41%.
- **Tests:** new checks for typed one-decimal HSL and for the swatch HSL text.

**Behavior you'll notice**

     ```ts
     import type { ColorEntry, PaletteParams, SatMode } from "../types/palette";
     import { roundPercent } from "./colors.ts";
     /**
      * One entry per integer lightness from lMin to lMax, light to dark. With
      * `count`, that many evenly spaced steps instead, rounded to 0.1 L (9 steps over
      * 0–100 land on 12.5, 37.5, …). A count that reaches the integer steps gets them all.
      */
     export function generateNeutrals(params: PaletteParams, count?: number): ColorEntry[] {
       const { hue, saturation, sMod, satMode, lMin, lMax } = params;
       const span = lMax - lMin;
       const steps =
         count === undefined || count > span
           ? Array.from({ length: span + 1 }, (_, i) => lMin + i)
           : Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) =>
               roundPercent(lMin + (i * span) / (count - 1)),
             );
       const entries: ColorEntry[] = [];
       for (const i of steps) {
         const l = i / 100;
         const sK = getSaturation(i, sMod, satMode);
         const color = chroma.hsl(hue, saturation * sK, l);
         const [h, s, lVal] = color.hsl();
         const hRound = Math.round(h) || 0;
         const sRound = roundPercent(s * 100);
         const lRound = roundPercent(lVal * 100);
         entries.push({ label: `grey-${i}`, lightness: i, hsl: [h, s, lVal],
           hslString: `${hRound} ${sRound}% ${lRound}%`, hex: color.hex() });
       }
       return entries.reverse();
     }
     ```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-05 01:23:41Z)**_

chroma.js rounds the color to 8-bit RGB before we read the hue back. When saturation is low, that rounding leaves only a few possible hues, and 220 isn't one of them.

**How it happens.** chroma converts `hsl()` to RGB and rounds each channel to a whole number from 0 to 255. `parseTargetColor` then works out the hue from those rounded channels, so the typed hue is already gone. It's the same loss the saturation fix worked around.

**Why low saturation makes it worse.** The hue comes from where the middle channel sits between the lowest and highest channels. For `hsl(220 2% 50%)`:

- Exact channels: R 124.95, G 126.65, B 130.05
- Rounded: R 125, G 127, B 130

B and R are only 5 apart, so each whole step of G moves the hue by 60° / 5 = 12°. The only hues possible there are 240, 228, 216, 204, 192 and 180. The closest to 220 is 216.

The gap between channels is about 255 × S × (1 − |2L − 1|). Low saturation shrinks it, and so does lightness far from 50%. At L10 the gap is a fifth of what it is at L50.

**Measured.** I ran every whole-degree hue through `parseTargetColor`. Each cell shows the worst error, then how many of the 360 hues came back wrong:

| S | L 50% | L 10% |
|---|---|---|
| 1% | 13° (342) | 30° (354) |
| 2% | 6° (330) | 30° (354) |
| 5% | 3° (282) | 13° (342) |
| 10% | 2° (210) | 6° (330) |
| 20% | 1° (54) | 4° (294) |
| 50% | 0° (0) | 2° (210) |

At 0% the hue is lost completely: `hsl(220 0% 50%)` comes back as hue 0.

**What you'd see.** `setTarget` puts the parsed hue straight into the store, so the palette's hue becomes 216. The picker shows `hsl(220 2% 50%) → hsl(216, 2%, 50%)`.
- At 2% saturation the swatches look the same either way. But 216 stays in the store, so if you raise saturation later, the whole palette is 4° off the hue you typed.
- With 0% saturation the hue resets to 0, so raising saturation later gives a red palette.
- Neutrals are this app's main use, so low-saturation input is the normal case here.

**Only `hsl()` input is affected.** For hex or rgb, 216 really is the hue of `rgb(125, 127, 130)`, so nothing is lost. An oklch hue is in a different color space, so there's no typed HSL hue to keep there either.

**Fix.** Use the same approach as the saturation fix: read the hue straight from the typed text.
- No unit conversion is needed. chroma only accepts plain numbers and `deg` for hue, and already rejects `turn`, `rad` and `grad` as invalid.
- Negative or over-360 hues need wrapping into 0–359. chroma already turns -140 and 580 into 220.
- It's about three lines plus a test, and it also fixes the 0% case.

Should I fix it on this branch, as part of the one-decimal commit, or leave it for a board task?

I fixed the hue shift. For `hsl()` input the hue is now read straight from what you typed, the same way saturation already was. `hsl(220 2% 50%)` now gives hue 220. `hsl(220 0% 50%)` also keeps 220 instead of resetting to 0.

All the code changes are in `app/src/lib/colors.ts`:
- The pattern that reads typed values now captures the hue as well as the saturation.
- `deg` is accepted, because it's the only hue unit chroma allows; `none` counts as 0.
- Hues outside 0–359 wrap around, so a typed `-140` or `580` becomes 220.
- `parseTargetColor` was already at the lint complexity limit of 12. Instead of adding branches, both the typed path and the chroma path now go through a single ternary.
- Hex, rgb, oklch and named colors behave as before.

```text
---
type: epic

# EPIC-0009: Migrate from chroma.js to culori

Replace chroma.js with [culori](https://github.com/Evercoder/culori) as the sole color library. After EPIC-0006 lands, chroma.js remains used in four areas: contrast checking (`colors.ts`), export format conversion (`export.ts`), About dialog (`About.tsx`), and the SaturationCurve comparison strip. Culori has first-class OKLCH support, better gamut mapping, and a smaller bundle (tree-shakeable).

## Scope

- Replace `chroma.contrast()` in `colors.ts` with culori's contrast utilities
- Replace `chroma(hex).css('hsl')` / `.oklch()` / etc. in `export.ts` with culori format conversions
- Replace `chroma.hsl()` calls in `About.tsx` (educational strips, ColorPickerPlane) with culori
- Replace `chroma.hsl()` in SaturationCurve comparison strip with culori
- Evaluate whether the custom OKLCH functions from TASK-0020 can be replaced by culori equivalents (or kept for zero-dependency core)
- Remove chroma.js dependency from `package.json`

## Blocked by

- EPIC-0006 (core OKLCH migration must land first — chroma.js is still load-bearing until then)
- EPIC-0008 (About dialog rewrite — avoid migrating chroma.js calls that will be rewritten anyway)

## Reference

- culori repo: https://github.com/Evercoder/culori
- Q7 answer in NOTE-0006 analysis: "A wholesale switch to culori is a future cleanup task, not a migration blocker"
```

```text
import chroma from "chroma-js";
import type { ColorEntry, ExportFormat, ColorSpace } from "../types/palette";

function colorValue(entry: ColorEntry, space: ColorSpace): string {
  const c = chroma(entry.hex);
  switch (space) {
    case "hsl":
      return `hsl(${entry.hslString})`;
    case "hex":
      return entry.hex;
    case "rgb": {
      const [r, g, b] = c.rgb();
      return `rgb(${r}, ${g}, ${b})`;
    }
    case "hcl": {
      const [h, c2, l] = c.hcl();
      const hR = Math.round(h || 0);
      const cR = Math.round((c2 || 0) * 10) / 10;
      const lR = Math.round(l * 10) / 10;
      return `hcl(${hR}, ${cR}, ${lR})`;
    }
    case "oklch": {
      const [l, c2, h] = c.oklch();
      const lR = Math.round(l * 1000) / 1000;
      const cR = Math.round((c2 || 0) * 1000) / 1000;
      const hR = Math.round(h || 0);
      return `oklch(${lR} ${cR} ${hR})`;
    }
  }
}

export function formatPalette(
  entries: ColorEntry[],
  format: ExportFormat,
  space: ColorSpace,
): string {
  switch (format) {
    case "css":
      return formatCSS(entries, space);
    case "tw4":
      return formatTailwindV4(entries, space);
    case "tw3":
      return formatTailwindV3(entries, space);
    case "scss":
      return formatSCSS(entries, space);
    case "js":
      return formatJS(entries, space);
    case "json":
      return formatJSON(entries, space);
    case "gpl":
      return formatGPL(entries);
    case "text":
      return formatText(entries, space);
  }
}

function formatCSS(entries: ColorEntry[], space: ColorSpace): string {
  const vars = entries
    .map((e) => `  --${e.label}: ${colorValue(e, space)};`)
    .join("\n");
  return `:root {\n${vars}\n}`;
}

function formatTailwindV4(entries: ColorEntry[], space: ColorSpace): string {
  const vars = entries
    .map((e) => `  --color-${e.label}: ${colorValue(e, space)};`)
    .join("\n");
  return `@theme {\n${vars}\n}`;
}

function formatTailwindV3(entries: ColorEntry[], space: ColorSpace): string {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  for (const e of entries) {
    lines.push(`        ${String(e.lightness)}: "${colorValue(e, space)}",`);
  }
  return [
    "/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */",
    "module.exports = {",
    "  theme: {",
    "    extend: {",
    "      colors: {",
    "        grey: {",
    ...lines,
    "        },",
    "      },",
    "    },",
    "  },",
    "};",
  ].join("\n");
}

function formatSCSS(entries: ColorEntry[], space: ColorSpace): string {
  return entries.map((e) => `$${e.label}: ${colorValue(e, space)};`).join("\n");
}

function formatJS(entries: ColorEntry[], space: ColorSpace): string {
  const colors: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const e of entries) {
    colors[String(e.lightness)] = colorValue(e, space);
  }
  return `export const grey = ${JSON.stringify(colors, null, 2)} as const;`;
}

function formatJSON(entries: ColorEntry[], space: ColorSpace): string {
  const tokens: Record<string, { $value: string; $type: string }> = {};
  for (const e of entries) {
    tokens[String(e.lightness)] = {
      $value: colorValue(e, space),
      $type: "color",
    };
  }
  return JSON.stringify({ grey: tokens }, null, 2);
}

function formatGPL(entries: ColorEntry[]): string {
  const lines = [
    "GIMP Palette",
    "Name: Grey Neutrals",
    `Columns: ${entries.length}`,
    "#",
  ];
  for (const e of entries) {
    const c = chroma(e.hex);
    const [r, g, b] = c.rgb();
    lines.push(
      `${String(Math.round(r)).padStart(3)} ${String(Math.round(g)).padStart(3)} ${String(Math.round(b)).padStart(3)}\t${e.label}`,
    );
  }
  return lines.join("\n");
}

function formatText(entries: ColorEntry[], space: ColorSpace): string {
  const maxLabel = Math.max(...entries.map((e) => e.label.length));
  return entries
    .map((e) => `${e.label.padEnd(maxLabel)}  ${colorValue(e, space)}`)
    .join("\n");
}

const FORMAT_EXTENSIONS: Record<ExportFormat, string> = {
  css: "css",
  tw4: "css",
  tw3: "js",
  scss: "scss",
  js: "ts",
  json: "json",
  gpl: "gpl",
  text: "txt",
};

const FORMAT_MIME_TYPES: Record<ExportFormat, string> = {
  css: "text/css",
  tw4: "text/css",
  tw3: "text/javascript",
  scss: "text/css",
  js: "text/javascript",
  json: "application/json",
  gpl: "text/plain",
  text: "text/plain",
};

export function downloadPalette(
  entries: ColorEntry[],
  format: ExportFormat,
  space: ColorSpace,
): void {
  const content = formatPalette(entries, format, space);
  const ext = FORMAT_EXTENSIONS[format];
  const mime = FORMAT_MIME_TYPES[format];
  const blob = new Blob([content], { type: `${mime};charset=utf-8` });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = `palette.${ext}`;
  a.click();
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}
```

```mjs
const LIBS = process.argv[2];

for (let r = 0; r < 256; r += 15)
  for (let g = 0; g < 256; g += 15)
    for (let b = 0; b < 256; b += 15) grid.add(`#${h2(r)}${h2(g)}${h2(b)}`);

      palette.push(e);
const hexes = [...new Set([...grid, ...palette.map((e) => e.hex)])];

const libs = {
  chroma: (hex) => chroma(hex).oklch(),
  culori: (hex) => {
    const c = toOk(hex);
    return [c.l, c.c, c.h];
  },
};
// The app's string format, with hue zeroed when chroma rounds to 0
const fmt = ([l, c, h], hueDp = 0, dp = 3) => {
  const k = 10 ** dp;
  const cR = Math.round((c || 0) * k) / k;
  const hR = cR ? Math.round((h || 0) * 10 ** hueDp) / 10 ** hueDp : 0;
  return `oklch(${Math.round(l * k) / k} ${cR} ${hR})`;
};
for (const [name, fn] of Object.entries(libs)) {
  let dL = 0, dC = 0, dH = 0, diffs = 0, grayHue = 0;

    const [l, c, h] = fn(hex);
    dL = Math.max(dL, Math.abs(l - L));
    dC = Math.max(dC, Math.abs((c || 0) - (C || 0)));
    if (C > 0.02) dH = Math.max(dH, Math.abs(((h - H + 540) % 360) - 180));
    if (fmt([l, c, h]) !== fmt([L, C, H])) diffs++;
    if (Math.round((c || 0) * 1000) === 0 && Math.round(h || 0) !== 0) grayHue++;
  }
  console.log(
    `A ${name} vs ref: max dL ${dL.toExponential(1)}, dC ${dC.toExponential(1)}, dH ${dH.toExponential(1)}°; ` +

const roundTrip = (pairs) => pairs.filter(([hex, css]) => refHex(css) !== hex).length;
const swatchPairs = palette.map((e) => [e.hex, toOklchString(e.hex)]);
const targetPairs = [];
for (let hue = 0; hue < 360; hue++)
  for (const s of [0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1])
    targetPairs.push([formatTargetColor(hue, s, "hex"), formatTargetColor(hue, s, "oklch")]);
console.log(`B oklch->hex mismatches: swatches ${roundTrip(swatchPairs)}/${swatchPairs.length}, target ${roundTrip(targetPairs)}/${targetPairs.length}`);
const precise = (pairs) =>
  roundTrip(pairs.map(([hex]) => [hex, fmt(libs.culori(hex), 1, 4)]));
console.log(`B with 4dp L/C + 0.1° hue: swatches ${precise(swatchPairs)}, target ${precise(targetPairs)}`);

// --- C. "hcl" export: chroma hcl (D65 LCh) vs CSS lch() (D50)
const ex = "#406abf";

  " CSS lch [l,c,h]:", new Color(ex).to("lch").coords.map((v) => +v.toFixed(2)),
  " culori lch:", (({ l, c, h }) => [l, c, h].map((v) => +v.toFixed(2)))(culori.lch(ex)));
let dLchL = 0, dLchC = 0;
for (const e of palette) {
  const [, c, l] = chroma(e.hex).hcl();
  const [L, C] = new Color(e.hex).to("lch").coords;
  dLchL = Math.max(dLchL, Math.abs(l - L));

}
console.log(`C palette max |chroma hcl - CSS lch|: L ${dLchL.toFixed(2)}, C ${dLchC.toFixed(2)}`);

  "hsl(0.5turn 50% 50%)", "hsla(220deg, 50%, 50%, 0.5)", "rgb(10% 20% 30%)",
  "rgb(10 20 30 / 50%)", "#4f8a", "#4f8af0cc", "hwb(220 10% 20%)", "lab(50% 20 -40)",
  "lch(50% 40 250)", "oklab(0.6 -0.05 -0.1)", "color(srgb 0.2 0.4 0.8)", "color(display-p3 0.2 0.4 0.8)",
];

// --- E. Out-of-sRGB input

  const r = parseTargetColor(s);
  const hue = culori.oklch(s).h;
  const clip = culori.oklch(culori.clampRgb(s)).h;
  const mapped = culori.oklch(toGamut(s)).h;
  console.log(`E ${s.padEnd(24)} app: ${JSON.stringify(r)}  oklch hue: input ${hue?.toFixed(1)}, clipped ${clip?.toFixed(1)}, CSS4-mapped ${mapped?.toFixed(1)}`);
}

// --- F. Contrast
let dCon = 0, below = 0, worse = 0, belowBest = 0;
for (const hex of hexes) {
  const c = new Color("white").contrast(hex, "WCAG21");
  dCon = Math.max(dCon, Math.abs(chroma.contrast("white", hex) - c), Math.abs(culori.wcagContrast("white", hex) - c));
}
for (const e of palette) {
  const pick = getContrastColor(e.hex);
  const other = pick === "#ffffff" ? "#1d1d1d" : "#ffffff";
  const cp = chroma.contrast(pick, e.hex);
  const co = chroma.contrast(other, e.hex);
  if (cp < 4.5) below++;
  if (co > cp) worse++;
  if (Math.max(chroma.contrast("#000", e.hex), chroma.contrast("#fff", e.hex)) < 4.5) belowBest++;
}
console.log(`F max contrast diff vs ref: ${dCon.toExponential(1)}; swatch labels under 4.5:1 ${below}/${palette.length}, other color better ${worse}, under 4.5 even with best of #000/#fff ${belowBest}`);
```

Partly. culori would fix real problems in chroma's conversions and parsing, and it's the right base for EPIC-0006. But the swatches wouldn't change, and the biggest accuracy problems I found are in our own code, which culori doesn't fix.

I measured chroma and culori against colorjs.io, which is written by the CSS Color 4 spec editors.

**What culori fixes**
- **OKLCH values:** chroma is off by up to 3.6e-5 in L and 0.11° in hue. That makes 1,151 of 19,006 oklch strings, at the app's precision, differ from the reference in the last digit. culori matches the reference exactly: 0 differ.
- **A hidden coupling in chroma:** its OKLab conversion goes through its Lab code, which uses a global white point. Switching that to D50, which correct CSS `lch()` needs, breaks OKLCH. For `#406abf`, chroma drops from the correct 0.141 to 0.103, about 27% low. With chroma you can't have correct `lch()` and correct `oklch()` at the same time; culori keeps them independent.
- **Parsing:** chroma rejects valid CSS that culori accepts: `hsl(0.5turn …)`, `hsla(220deg, …)`, `hwb()`, `color(srgb …)` and `color(display-p3 …)`. culori also keeps the input's own color space without 8-bit rounding, so the hsl regex workaround we just added could go away.
- **Gamut mapping:** chroma can only clip colors that fall outside sRGB. culori implements the CSS Color 4 gamut-mapping method, within 1.2/255 of the reference across 4,104 colors. EPIC-0006 needs this to find the highest in-gamut chroma for each lightness and hue.

**What wouldn't change**
- **Palette hex:** identical for 266,375 of 266,640 inputs. The other 265 are channels that land exactly on .5, where tiny floating-point differences round them in opposite directions.
- **WCAG contrast:** both libraries are within 0.001 of the reference.

**Problems in our code that culori won't fix**
1. **Target mode distorts colors.** Saturation times the curve multiplier can go above 100%. Converting that to RGB pushes channels out of range, and clipping them shifts hue and lightness. culori would clip the same way.
   - With saturation 50% and the curve at −96%, `grey-10` renders as `hsl(240 100% 47.5%)` and `grey-90` as `hsl(204 100% 52.5%)`.
   - With the default curve and saturation 100%, `grey-10` is `hsl(226 100% 11.8%)`.
   - Fix: cap saturation at 100% in `generateNeutrals`, which keeps hue and lightness exact.
2. **OKLCH strings don't convert back to their own hex.** At 3 decimals and a whole-degree hue, 11% of swatch strings and 55% of target strings convert back to a hex one step off in a channel. You can't see it, but the formats disagree. Both libraries give the same counts:

   | L/C decimals | Hue decimals | Strings that miss their hex |
   |---|---|---|
   | 3 | 0 (current) | 49% |
   | 4 | 2 | 0.09% |
   | 5 | 2 | 0% |

   More decimals means noisier strings, so how much precision to show is your call.
3. **The "HCL" export isn't valid CSS.** It writes `hcl(285, 50.8, 45.9)` into CSS, SCSS and Tailwind files, and browsers drop it. The numbers also use chroma's D65 white point instead of CSS `lch()`'s D50: `#406abf` has hue 285.2 versus 277.8 in CSS `lch()`. Across the palette samples, L is off by up to 1.6 and C by up to 5.0. It should export real `lch()`.
4. **Swatch labels miss AA contrast.** 710 of 14,544 swatches (4.9%) get label text below 4.5:1. The rule switches to `#1d1d1d` whenever white is below 4.5, even when white is still the better choice; 359 swatches got the worse of the two. Choosing whichever of black or white contrasts more would put every swatch at 4.5:1 or above.
5. **Minor:** `lch()`, `lab()` and `oklab()` target input is detected as format "named", so the target row echoes it back as hex.

**Board**
- EPIC-0009's list of where chroma is used is out of date. The files are now `AboutButton.tsx` and `ChartTabs.tsx`, not `About.tsx` and a SaturationCurve strip.
- EPIC-0006 plans custom OKLCH functions (TASK-0020) and moves to culori later. That builds the gamut math twice. I'd bring culori in with EPIC-0006 instead.

I'd fix items 1–4 now, since they don't depend on the library, and adopt culori as part of the OKLCH migration. The measurement scripts are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-grant-code-chroma-curve/ded7e9a5-fc33-4fd6-abcf-02d5d22c0219/scratchpad/scripts/`.

Should I add board tasks for items 1–4, and update EPIC-0006 and EPIC-0009 so culori comes in with the OKLCH migration?

       - The output `hcl(h, c, l)` is not valid CSS.

       - culori `lch` matches CSS exactly.
     - OKLCH string precision bug (ours, independent of library):
       - With 3 decimals on L/C and integer hue, the string fails to round-trip to its hex for 1594/14544 swatches (11%) and 797/1440 targets (55%), using the reference parser.
       - Over 154,690 colors: 3/0 decimals give ~76k mismatches for both libraries; 4/1 ~4.8k; 4/2 133–139; 5/1 ~4.3k; 5/2 gives 0 for both.
     - Target-mode clipping bug (ours):
       - `saturation * sK > 1` makes chroma clip RGB per channel, which shifts hue and lightness.
       - S=0.5, sMod=26: grey-10 → #0000f2 = hsl(240 100% 47.5%), grey-90 → hsl(204 100% 52.5%), grey-20 → #0000ff.
       - S=1, sMod=70: grey-10 → hsl(226 100% 11.8%), grey-90 → hsl(217 100% 88.2%).
       - Fix: clamp `Math.min(1, saturation * sK)`. culori would clip the same way, so it doesn't fix this.
     - Parsing:
       - The app rejects `hsl(0.5turn …)`, `hsla(220deg, …)`, `hwb()`, `color(srgb …)` and `color(display-p3 …)`. culori accepts all of them.
       - `lch(...)` input is detected as format "named".
     - Out-of-sRGB input:
       - `oklch(70% 0.3 240)` → app hue 201, sat 1 via clipping. OKLCH hue: clipped 244.0, CSS4-mapped 242.4.
       - `lch(50% 130 250)`: clipped hue 250.7 vs mapped 194.6.
       - culori `toGamut` matches the colorjs CSS gamut mapping within 1.169/255 over 4104 colors.
     - Contrast rule (ours):
       - 710/14544 swatch labels are under 4.5:1. In 359 of those, the other text color would be better.
       - Using the best of #000/#fff gives 0 under 4.5. The #1d1d1d dark text caps mid-tone contrast at ~4.1.
     - Mixed sources: the hsl export comes from the floats, while oklch and rgb come from the 8-bit hex.
     - Future (EPIC-0006): OKLCH generation needs a gamut boundary, gamut mapping and maybe P3. culori has spec-aligned, tested versions, whereas chroma has none (it only clips).

Before creating, check if a similar item already exists. If a close match is found, ask the user if they still want to create a new one.

## Scope Assessment

When the user requests a **TASK**, evaluate whether it is actually EPIC-sized before creating it. Look for these signals:

- Multiple distinct steps or deliverables in the description
- Multiple action verbs joined by "and" (e.g., "add auth and set up roles and integrate SSO")
- Work that spans different code areas or concerns
- Sub-steps that could be completed and shipped independently

**Quick test:** "Could someone meaningfully complete and ship part of this while the rest remains undone?" If yes → likely an EPIC.

If EPIC signals are present, suggest an EPIC + sub-TASKs with a concrete breakdown. For example:

> "This looks like it has multiple independent deliverables. Want me to create an EPIC with separate TASKs for each piece instead?"

**This is a soft suggestion only.** If the user says "just make it a task," comply without pushback.

This assessment only applies to TASK creation — do not second-guess EPICs, NOTEs, or other types.

## Arguments

The user provides the type and title: `/board:board-add task <title>`, `/board:board-add epic <title>`, etc.

If no type is given, ask the user what type of item to create.

Run the ID assignment script:

```bash
bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/gdkeller/board/0.1.0/scripts/next-id.sh" <TYPE> ./board
```

This scans all directories (including `board/archive/` and `.doc-ids`) and returns the next available 4-digit zero-padded ID.

```text
# TASK-0100: Improve swatch-label legibility on mid-tone backgrounds

Swatch labels (hex/HSL/OKLCH values) auto-switch between dark and light text based on background lightness, but the L30–70 mid-tone range produces marginal contrast in either direction. The HSL-value type size also drops below comfortable reading at small swatch sizes.

## Acceptance

- Mid-tone backgrounds (L30–70) reach WCAG AA contrast for label text — via text-shadow, a subtle backing pill, or a guaranteed-legible token rather than auto-switch.
- Minimum HSL-value font size raised to a comfortable floor.
- Existing dark/light auto-switch preserved for clear-cut cases.

# EPIC-0006: Migrate palette generation from HSL to OKLCH

Migrate all internal color math from HSL to OKLCH. The parabolic correction curve shifts from a necessity (compensating for HSL's perceptual brokenness) to an opt-in artistic refinement. Gamut-aware chroma clamping replaces hard clipping. Hue-dependent center shift makes the curve smarter.

## Scope

- OKLCH conversion functions (custom, not culori — keep chroma-js for non-generation uses)
- Memoized sRGB gamut boundary lookup (per-hue cache, 101 lightness steps)
- Hue-dependent chroma correction with both endpoint and target satMode
- Hue-aware saturation→chroma slider mapping (100% = max gamut chroma for current hue)
- Refactored `generateNeutrals` producing OKLCH internally, deriving HSL/hex at output
- Labels stay `grey-{0–100}` (OKLCH lightness scaled to integer)
- Visual tuning of default sMod for OKLCH context

## Key decisions

- **satMode** carries forward (both endpoint and target)
- **chroma-js** stays for contrast, export conversion, About — OKLCH math is additive
- **sMod/p** parameter mapping unchanged (`pctToSMod` stays as-is)
- **Curve defaults to on** — hue-dependent center shift is the new default experience
- **About dialog** is a separate deferred effort (EPIC-0008)

## Reference

- REFE-0003: OKLCH color math — conversion functions, gamut search, peak-lightness table, correction formula
- NOTE-0006 *(archived)*: Original migration guide, including the "what changes / what doesn't" decisions and the migration checklist
- REFE-0001: Parabolic saturation curve background

# EPIC-0009: Migrate from chroma.js to culori

Replace chroma.js with [culori](https://github.com/Evercoder/culori) as the sole color library. After EPIC-0006 lands, chroma.js remains used in four areas: contrast checking (`colors.ts`), export format conversion (`export.ts`), About dialog (`About.tsx`), and the SaturationCurve comparison strip. Culori has first-class OKLCH support, better gamut mapping, and a smaller bundle (tree-shakeable).

## Scope

- Replace `chroma.contrast()` in `colors.ts` with culori's contrast utilities
- Replace `chroma(hex).css('hsl')` / `.oklch()` / etc. in `export.ts` with culori format conversions
- Replace `chroma.hsl()` calls in `About.tsx` (educational strips, ColorPickerPlane) with culori
- Replace `chroma.hsl()` in SaturationCurve comparison strip with culori
- Evaluate whether the custom OKLCH functions from TASK-0020 can be replaced by culori equivalents (or kept for zero-dependency core)
- Remove chroma.js dependency from `package.json`

## Blocked by

- EPIC-0006 (core OKLCH migration must land first — chroma.js is still load-bearing until then)
- EPIC-0008 (About dialog rewrite — avoid migrating chroma.js calls that will be rewritten anyway)

## Reference

- culori repo: https://github.com/Evercoder/culori
- Q7 answer in NOTE-0006 analysis: "A wholesale switch to culori is a future cleanup task, not a migration blocker"
```

```text
     1	import chroma from "chroma-js";
     2	import type { ColorEntry, PaletteParams, SatMode } from "../types/palette";
     3	import { roundPercent } from "./colors.ts";
     4	
     5	/**
     6	 * Parabolic saturation curve centered at lightness 50%.
     7	 * See: https://www.desmos.com/calculator/02ufrfsuzy
     8	 *
     9	 * In "endpoint" mode the multiplier is 1.0 at L0/L100 (slider = endpoint saturation).
    10	 * In "target" mode the multiplier is 1.0 at L50 (slider = vertex/target saturation).
    11	 */
    12	export function getSaturation(
    13	  lightness: number,
    14	  sMod: number,
    15	  satMode: SatMode,
    16	): number {
    17	  if (sMod === 0) return 1;
    18	  const o = 50;
    19	  const raw =
    20	    1 + (Math.pow(lightness - o, 2) / sMod - Math.pow(o, 2) / sMod) / 100;
    21	
    22	  if (satMode === "endpoint") return raw;
    23	
    24	  // Normalize so vertex (L50) = 1.0, endpoints > 1.0
    25	  const vertex = 1 - Math.pow(o, 2) / sMod / 100;
    26	  if (vertex <= 0) return raw;
    27	  return raw / vertex;
    28	}
    29	
    30	/**
    31	 * One entry per integer lightness from lMin to lMax, light to dark. With
    32	 * `count`, that many evenly spaced steps instead, rounded to 0.1 L (9 steps over
    33	 * 0–100 land on 12.5, 37.5, …). A count that reaches the integer steps gets them all.
    34	 */
    35	export function generateNeutrals(
    36	  params: PaletteParams,
    37	  count?: number,
    38	): ColorEntry[] {
    39	  const { hue, saturation, sMod, satMode, lMin, lMax } = params;
    40	  const span = lMax - lMin;
    41	  const steps =
    42	    count === undefined || count > span
    43	      ? Array.from({ length: span + 1 }, (_, i) => lMin + i)
    44	      : Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) =>
    45	          roundPercent(lMin + (i * span) / (count - 1)),
    46	        );
    47	
    48	  const entries: ColorEntry[] = [];
    49	
    50	  for (const i of steps) {
    51	    const l = i / 100;
    52	    const sK = getSaturation(i, sMod, satMode);
    53	    const color = chroma.hsl(hue, saturation * sK, l);
    54	
    55	    const [h, s, lVal] = color.hsl();
    56	    const hRound = Math.round(h) || 0;
    57	    const sRound = roundPercent(s * 100);
    58	    const lRound = roundPercent(lVal * 100);
    59	
    60	    entries.push({
    61	      label: `grey-${i}`,
    62	      lightness: i,
    63	      hsl: [h, s, lVal],
    64	      hslString: `${hRound} ${sRound}% ${lRound}%`,
    65	      hex: color.hex(),
    66	    });
    67	  }
    68	
    69	  return entries.reverse();
    70	}

     4	function colorValue(entry: ColorEntry, space: ColorSpace): string {

     6	  switch (space) {
     7	    case "hsl":

     9	    case "hex":

    11	    case "rgb": {

    13	      return `rgb(${r}, ${g}, ${b})`;

    15	    case "hcl": {

    18	      const cR = Math.round((c2 || 0) * 10) / 10;
    19	      const lR = Math.round(l * 10) / 10;

    24	      const lR = Math.round(l * 1000) / 1000;
    25	      const cR = Math.round((c2 || 0) * 1000) / 1000;
    26	      const hR = Math.round(h || 0);
    27	      return `oklch(${lR} ${cR} ${hR})`;
```

## Validation Rules

### Status Transitions

Validate transitions using the script:

```bash
bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/gdkeller/board/0.1.0/scripts/validate-status.sh" <type> <from_status> <to_status>
```

Exit codes: `0` = valid forward transition, `2` = backward transition (confirm with user), `1` = invalid.

Valid forward transitions:

| Type | Valid Transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| task | `backlog` → `current` → `done` |
| epic | `planning` → `current` → `done` |
| resource | `inbox` → `processing` → `processed` |
| note | `inbox` → `processed` |
| adr | `active` → `superseded` or `active` → `deprecated` |

Backward transitions (e.g., `done` → `backlog`) are allowed but should confirm with the user first — they may indicate a reopened task.

### ADR Immutability

ADRs are **immutable**. The only permitted edit is changing `status` (to `superseded` or `deprecated`). If the user asks to edit ADR content, explain that ADRs are write-once and suggest:
- Adding a dated addendum at the bottom of the file
- Creating a new ADR that supersedes the old one (via `/board:board-add adr`)

If setting an ADR to `superseded`, ask for the superseding ADR ID and add `superseded_by` to the frontmatter.

### Task Title Changes

If editing a task title (the `# heading` or filename), enforce imperative mood. If the new title is a noun phrase, rewrite it (e.g., "authentication" → "Add authentication").

Renaming also requires renaming the file to match: `TASK-NNNN_new-kebab-case-title.md`. Use `git mv` to preserve history.

### Reference Docs

REFE items have no status field. Edits to reference content are unrestricted — they are meant to be kept current.

### Priority Values

Only `1` (high), `2` (medium), or `3` (low) are valid. Reject other values.

## Editable Fields

| Field | Types | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| `status` | all except reference | Must follow valid transitions |
| `priority` | task | Values: 1, 2, 3 |
| `blocked_by` | task | List of task IDs; add or remove individual blockers |
| `parent` | task | Link to parent epic |
| `due` | task | Date value |
| `tags` | all | List of strings; add or remove individual tags |
| `title` | all | Rename heading + file; imperative mood for tasks |
| `body` | all except adr | Freeform content below frontmatter |
| `superseded_by` | adr | Only when setting status to superseded |
| `url` | resource | Primary external URL |
| `type` | all except adr | Retype/convert — creates new file, deletes old (see below) |

## Retype (Convert Type)

When the user asks to convert or retype an item (e.g., "convert TASK-0022 to a note", "retype this as an epic"):

### Validation

1. **Refuse if source is ADR** — ADRs are immutable. Explain why and suggest creating a new item separately.
2. **Confirm with user** — "This will delete TASK-0022 and create a new NOTE with the next available ID. Proceed?"

### Procedure

1. **Get next ID** for the target type:
   ```bash
   bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/gdkeller/board/0.1.0/scripts/next-id.sh" <TARGET_TYPE> ./board
   ```
2. **Create new file** with:
   - Correct type prefix and ID in filename
   - Correct directory for the target type
   - Correct frontmatter (initial status for new type, carry over applicable fields)
   - Body content carried over from old item
   - Title adjusted if needed (e.g., imperative mood for TASKs, relaxed for NOTEs)
3. **Delete old file** via `git rm`
4. **Find and update cross-references** — use Grep to search for the old ID across all board files:
   - `blocked_by` lists
   - `parent` fields
   - `tasks` lists (in EPICs)
   - `spawned` lists (in NOTEs)
   - Wiki-links (`[[OLD-ID]]`) in body content

   Update each reference to the new ID.
5. **Report** the change: `Retyped: TASK-0022 → NOTE-0005 (old file deleted, references updated)`

### Type-Specific Adjustments

| Target Type | Adjustments |
|-------------|-------------|
| task | Title must be imperative mood; `status: backlog`; add `priority: 2` |
| epic | Title stays imperative; `status: planning`; consider adding `tasks:` list |
| note | `status: inbox`; title can relax imperative mood |
| reference | No status field; content must be objective/encyclopedic |
| resource | Requires `url` (ask user); `status: inbox` |

## Execution

1. Apply the edit via targeted frontmatter field replacement (use Edit tool, not full file rewrite)
2. If renaming, use `git mv` for the file and update the `# heading`
3. **If the status change results in a terminal status** (`done` for tasks/epics, `processed` for resources/notes), archive the item immediately after updating the status:
   ```bash
   bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/gdkeller/board/0.1.0/scripts/archive-batch.sh" ./board <file_path>
   ```
   ADRs are the sole exception — they are never archived regardless of status.
   If the user explicitly asks NOT to archive, respect that but note the lint warning they will see.
4. Show a summary of what changed: `TASK-0003: status backlog → done → archived`
5. If the edit unblocks other tasks (a blocker was marked `done`), mention which tasks are now unblocked

## Notes

- **Avoid redundant invocations** — if this skill was already invoked earlier in the session and the board has not been modified since, reuse the previous board data instead of invoking again

```text
export function ChartTabs({ entries }: ChartTabsProps) {
  const [showDots, setShowDots] = useState(true);
  const [showCompare, setShowCompare] = useState(false);
  const hue = usePaletteStore((s) => s.hue);
  const saturation = usePaletteStore((s) => s.saturation);

  const { unadjustedColors, adjustedColors } = useMemo(
    () => ({
      unadjustedColors: entries.map((e) =>
        chroma.hsl(hue, saturation, e.lightness / 100).hex(),
      ),
      adjustedColors: entries.map((e) => e.hex),
    }),
    [entries, hue, saturation],
  );

  return (
    <div className="border-border-default bg-surface-raised mx-4 overflow-hidden rounded-none border md:mx-0 lg:mr-4">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between px-4 py-2 md:hidden lg:flex">
        <h2 className="text-text-muted w-full text-center text-sm font-semibold tracking-wider uppercase">
          Saturation Curve
----ColorSwatch
export function ColorSwatch({
  entry,
  copyFormat,
  isCopied,
  onCopy,
  showLabels = true,
  tall = false,
}: ColorSwatchProps) {
  const textColor = getContrastColor(entry.hex);
  const oklch = toOklchString(entry.hex);

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      className={`focus-visible:ring-offset-surface-base group relative flex cursor-pointer flex-col justify-start gap-1 px-2 py-1.5 text-left focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-white/50 focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-none ${tall ? "min-h-[240px]" : "min-h-[120px]"}`}
      style={{ backgroundColor: entry.hex, color: textColor }}
      onClick={() => onCopy(getCopyValue(entry, copyFormat), entry.label)}
      title={`${entry.label} - click to copy ${copyFormat.toUpperCase()}`}
    >
      {showLabels && (
        <>
          <span className="mb-4 origin-left text-sm font-semibold transition-transform group-hover:scale-105">

          <span className="text-sm">{entry.hex}</span>
          <span className="text-2xs">hsl({entry.hslString})</span>
          <span className="text-2xs">{oklch}</span>
        </>
      )}
      <CopyFeedback visible={isCopied} />
    </button>
```

```mjs
// Facts for the board tasks. Usage: node task-facts.mjs <libs/node_modules>
const APP = "/Users/grant/code/chroma-curve/app";
const LIBS = process.argv[2];
const chroma = (await import(`${APP}/node_modules/chroma-js/index.js`)).default;
const culori = await import(`${LIBS}/culori/src/index.js`);
const Color = (await import(`${LIBS}/colorjs.io/src/index.js`)).default;
const { generateNeutrals } = await import(`${APP}/src/lib/palette.ts`);

const h2 = (n) => n.toString(16).padStart(2, "0");
const hexes = new Set();
const palette = [];
for (let hue = 0; hue < 360; hue += 10)
  for (const saturation of [0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1])
    for (const e of generateNeutrals({ hue, saturation, sMod: 70, satMode: "endpoint", lMin: 0, lMax: 100 })) {
      palette.push(e);
      hexes.add(e.hex);
    }
for (let r = 0; r < 256; r += 5)
  for (let g = 0; g < 256; g += 5)
    for (let b = 0; b < 256; b += 5) hexes.add(`#${h2(r)}${h2(g)}${h2(b)}`);
const all = [...hexes];
const refHex = (css) =>
  "#" + new Color(css).to("srgb").coords.map((v) => h2(Math.round(Math.min(1, Math.max(0, v || 0)) * 255))).join("");
const r = (v, dp) => Math.round((v || 0) * 10 ** dp) / 10 ** dp;

// a. chroma lch with the D50 white point vs CSS lch()
console.log("a whitepoint before:", chroma.getLabWhitePoint());
chroma.setLabWhitePoint("D50");
let dL = 0, dC = 0, dH = 0;
for (const hex of all) {
  const [l, c, h] = chroma(hex).lch();
  const [L, C, H] = new Color(hex).to("lch").coords;
  dL = Math.max(dL, Math.abs(l - L));
  dC = Math.max(dC, Math.abs((c || 0) - (C || 0)));
  if (C > 1) dH = Math.max(dH, Math.abs(((h - H + 540) % 360) - 180));
}
chroma.setLabWhitePoint("D65");
console.log(`a chroma D50 lch vs CSS lch over ${all.length}: max dL ${dL.toExponential(1)}, dC ${dC.toExponential(1)}, dH ${dH.toExponential(1)}`);
console.log("a whitepoint after reset:", chroma.getLabWhitePoint(), chroma("#406abf").oklch().map((v) => +v.toFixed(5)));

// b. lch() string precision needed to reproduce the hex
const toLch = culori.converter("lch");
for (const [lcDp, hDp] of [[1, 0], [2, 0], [2, 1], [2, 2], [3, 2]]) {
  const bad = all.filter((hex) => {
    const { l, c, h } = toLch(hex);
    return refHex(`lch(${r(l, lcDp)}% ${r(c, lcDp)} ${r(h, hDp)})`) !== hex;
  }).length;
  console.log(`b lch L/C ${lcDp}dp, hue ${hDp}dp: ${bad}/${all.length} mismatches`);
}

// c. pure grays at 5 decimals: chroma and culori chroma/hue
const toOk = culori.converter("oklch");
let maxGrayC = 0, grayHue = 0;
for (let v = 0; v < 256; v++) {
  const hex = `#${h2(v)}${h2(v)}${h2(v)}`;
  const [, c, h] = chroma(hex).oklch();
  const k = toOk(hex);
  maxGrayC = Math.max(maxGrayC, c || 0, k.c || 0);
  if (r(c, 5) === 0 && r(h, 2) !== 0) grayHue++;
}
console.log(`c grays: max C ${maxGrayC.toExponential(1)}; 5dp C=0 with nonzero chroma hue: ${grayHue}`);

// d. contrast: best of #1d1d1d/#fff, and darkest-text threshold for AA everywhere
const con = (a, b) => culori.wcagContrast(a, b);
let below1d = 0;
for (const e of palette) if (Math.max(con("#1d1d1d", e.hex), con("#ffffff", e.hex)) < 4.5) below1d++;
console.log(`d best of #1d1d1d/#fff under 4.5: ${below1d}/${palette.length}`);
const lum = (v) => culori.wcagLuminance(`#${h2(v)}${h2(v)}${h2(v)}`);
let maxV = -1;
for (let v = 0; v < 256; v++) if (Math.sqrt(1.05 / (lum(v) + 0.05)) >= 4.5) maxV = v;
const worst1d = Math.sqrt(1.05 / (lum(0x1d) + 0.05));
console.log(`d darkest gray with AA on every background: #${h2(maxV).repeat(3)}; #1d1d1d worst case ${worst1d.toFixed(2)}:1; #000 worst case ${Math.sqrt(1.05 / 0.05).toFixed(2)}:1`);
```

```markdown
# TASK-0133: Clamp target-mode saturation at 100%

In `target` satMode, `getSaturation()` divides by the L50 vertex, so the multiplier rises above 1 toward both ends. `generateNeutrals()` (`app/src/lib/palette.ts:53`) passes `saturation * sK` to `chroma.hsl()` without a cap. Above 100% saturation, HSL→RGB produces channels outside 0–255, and chroma clips each channel on its own. That shifts hue and lightness as well as saturation.

With the default adjustment (sMod 70), any saturation above 65.2% clips. For a requested hue of 220:

- **Saturation 100%:** 98 of 99 steps clip (all but L50). grey-10 renders as `hsl(226 100% 11.8%)` and grey-90 as `hsl(217 100% 88.2%)`.
- **Saturation 80%:** 32 steps clip, and hue moves by up to 4.1°.
- **Saturation 50% at the strongest adjustment (sMod 26):** 78 steps clip. grey-27 renders as pure blue, `hsl(240 100% 50%)`, and lightness is off by up to 39 points.

Endpoint mode is unaffected: its multiplier never exceeds 1. With the cap, high saturations flatten at 100% toward the ends, which is the real ceiling of HSL.

## Acceptance

- Effective saturation is `Math.min(1, saturation * sK)`, computed in one shared helper in `palette.ts`.
- `generateNeutrals()` and the Effective Saturation chart (`EffectiveSaturation.tsx:23,35`) both use the helper, so the chart shows what the swatches render.
- Unit test: in target mode with saturation above 0, every entry from L1 to L99 keeps the requested hue and its step's lightness, at any saturation and adjustment.

## Source

- Color-accuracy review of EPIC-0009, 2026-11-04

```

```markdown
# TASK-0135: Replace the hcl() export with CSS lch()

The export dialog's HCL color space writes values like `hcl(285, 50.8, 45.9)`. CSS has no `hcl()` function, so browsers drop every CSS, Tailwind and SCSS declaration that uses it. The numbers are not CSS LCh either: chroma's `hcl()` uses a D65 white point, and CSS `lch()` uses D50. For `#406abf`, chroma gives hue 285.2 and CSS `lch()` gives 277.8. Across sampled palettes, L differs by up to 1.6 and C by up to 5.0.

## Change

- Rename the `ColorSpace` value `hcl` to `lch` in `types/palette.ts:30`, `FormatSelector.tsx:25` (label "LCH") and `export.ts:15–21`. The selected space is local `ExportDialog` state, so nothing persisted needs migrating.
- Convert with culori's `lch` mode. It is CSS's D50 LCh and matches the reference exactly. Grays come back with chroma 0 and no hue.
- Format as `lch(L% C H)` with 2 decimals on each value. That reproduces every hex in a 153,328-color sample. With 1 decimal on hue, 4,126 (2.7%) miss.

## Why not chroma.js

chroma.js reaches D50 LCh only through `chroma.setLabWhitePoint("D50")`. That setting is global and also changes its OKLCH output: `#406abf` drops from C 0.141 to 0.103. Even with D50 set, chroma's LCh is off from the reference by up to 0.012 in C.

## Acceptance

- Exported `lch()` strings are valid CSS and parse back to each swatch's hex.
- `#406abf` exports as `lch(45.13% 50.44 277.82)`.
- No `hcl` remains in `app/src`.

## Source

- Color-accuracy review of EPIC-0009, 2026-11-04. Measured against colorjs.io 0.7.1, the CSS Color 4 reference implementation.
```

```markdown
# EPIC-0009: Migrate from chroma.js to culori

Make [culori](https://github.com/Evercoder/culori) the only color library and remove chroma.js. culori arrives with EPIC-0006 (TASK-0020) for OKLCH math; this epic moves the remaining chroma.js calls over. culori is more accurate than chroma.js, parses all of CSS Color 4, maps out-of-gamut colors the way CSS does, and is tree-shakeable. See EPIC-0006, "Why culori", for the measurements.

Swapping libraries doesn't change today's palettes: HSL→hex is identical for 266,375 of 266,640 inputs, and the other 265 are exact .5 channel ties.

## chroma.js call sites (2026-11-04)

- `lib/colors.ts`: label contrast (`getContrastColor`), target-color parsing and formatting
- `lib/export.ts`: export conversions (TASK-0134 and TASK-0135 move `oklch()` and `lch()` to culori first)
- `lib/palette.ts`: HSL generation, replaced by EPIC-0006 (TASK-0024)
- `components/TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`: target preview canvas
- `components/ChartTabs/ChartTabs.tsx`: unadjusted Compare strip
- `components/AboutButton/AboutButton.tsx`: educational strips, rewritten by EPIC-0008

## Scope

- Replace `chroma.contrast()` with culori's `wcagContrast`. Results match: both are within 0.001 of the reference.
- Parse target-color input with culori's `parse`. It accepts CSS Color 4 syntax that chroma.js rejects: `turn`, `rad` and `grad` hue units, comma-syntax `hsla()` with `deg`, `hwb()`, and `color(srgb …)` / `color(display-p3 …)`. It keeps typed values unrounded, so the `HSL_TOKENS` workaround in `colors.ts` can go.
- Detect the input format from culori's parsed mode. Today `lch()`, `lab()` and `oklab()` input is detected as format "named", so the target row echoes it back as hex.
- Gamut-map out-of-sRGB input with culori's `toGamut` instead of chroma.js's per-channel clipping. Clipping `lch(50% 130 250)` lands on OKLCH hue 250.7, 56° from the input's 194.2. CSS Color 4 mapping keeps it at 194.6.
- Replace `chroma.hsl()` in `TargetSwatch.tsx`, `ChartTabs.tsx` and, after EPIC-0008, `AboutButton.tsx`.
- Remove `chroma-js` and `@types/chroma-js` from `app/package.json`.

## Blocked by

- TASK-0020 (adds culori). Contrast and parsing can move as soon as it lands.
- EPIC-0006 before removing chroma.js: `palette.ts` generates with it until TASK-0024.
- EPIC-0008 for `AboutButton.tsx`: avoid migrating calls the rewrite replaces.

- culori repo: https://github.com/Evercoder/culori

- Q7 answer in NOTE-0006 analysis *(superseded 2026-11-04)*: "A wholesale switch to culori is a future cleanup task, not a migration blocker"
```

```markdown
# TASK-0134: Make oklch() strings reproduce their hex

`toOklchString()` (`app/src/lib/colors.ts:83`) rounds L and C to 3 decimals and hue to a whole degree. That is too coarse to pin down an 8-bit color. Parsed back with the CSS Color 4 reference, the string lands on a different hex for 11% of swatches (1,594 of 14,544) and 55% of target rows (797 of 1,440). Each miss is one step in one channel, so nobody sees it, but the copied `oklch()` and hex no longer describe the same color.

`export.ts:22–28` repeats the same formatting. Swatch labels, swatch copy, the target row and every export should share one formatter.

Precision measured over 154,690 colors (palettes, target rows and a 52³ RGB grid), converting with culori:

| L/C decimals | Hue decimals | Strings that miss their hex |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0 (current) | 76,098 (49.2%) |
| 4 | 1 | 4,771 (3.1%) |
| 4 | 2 | 139 (0.09%) |
| 5 | 1 | 4,328 (2.8%) |
| 5 | 2 | 0 |

## Why culori (blocked by TASK-0020)

chroma.js's OKLCH is off from the reference by up to 3.9e-5, which shows in the 5th decimal. It also gives pure grays a nonzero chroma (`#808080` → C 0.0000233), so at 5 decimals 248 of 256 grays would print a spurious chroma. culori matches the reference and returns chroma 0 for grays.

## Acceptance

- One `oklch()` formatter, used by `ColorSwatch` (label and copy value), `formatTargetColor()` and `export.ts`.
- Precision decided: 5 decimals on L/C and 2 on hue reproduce every hex; 4 and 2 give shorter strings and miss 0.09%.
- Unit test: each swatch's `oklch()` string parses back to its own hex.
- Grays print chroma 0 and hue 0.

## Related

- TASK-0029, TASK-0030: switch the source to native OKLCH floats after the migration, and keep this formatter.

## Source

- Color-accuracy review of EPIC-0009, 2026-11-04. Measured against colorjs.io 0.7.1, the CSS Color 4 reference implementation.
```

```markdown
# EPIC-0022: Make color values exact across the pipeline

Every value the app shows, copies or exports should describe the same color, follow the CSS Color 4 math, and be valid CSS. A review on 2026-11-04 measured the pipeline against colorjs.io 0.7.1, written by the CSS Color 4 editors, and found gaps at each stage:

- **Generation:** target mode clips saturation above 100%, which moves hue and lightness (TASK-0133).
- **Input:** target input rejects valid CSS Color 4 syntax and clips out-of-sRGB colors instead of gamut-mapping them (TASK-0136).
- **Output:** `oklch()` strings are too coarse to reproduce their hex (TASK-0134), and the HCL export isn't valid CSS (TASK-0135).

This epic holds the work that changes output. Library swaps that don't change output stay in EPIC-0009.

## Order

- TASK-0020 first: it adds culori. TASK-0134, TASK-0135 and TASK-0136 wait on it, as do EPIC-0006's TASK-0021, TASK-0022 and TASK-0024.
- TASK-0133 has no blockers.

## Why culori (2026-11-04)

Against the same reference:

- **Conversion:** culori's OKLCH matches the reference to 1e-16. chroma.js is off by up to 3.6e-5 in L, 3.9e-5 in C and 0.11° in hue, and gives pure grays a nonzero chroma.
- **Independent spaces:** chroma.js routes OKLab through its Lab white point, a global setting. Setting it to D50 for CSS `lch()` drops `#406abf` from C 0.141 to 0.103. culori keeps each space separate.
- **Parsing:** culori's `parse` accepts all CSS Color 4 syntax. chroma.js rejects `turn`, `rad` and `grad` hue units, `hwb()` and `color()`, and rounds `hsl()` input to 8-bit RGB.
- **Gamut mapping:** chroma.js only clips per channel. culori's `toGamut` implements the CSS Color 4 method (within 1.2/255 of the reference over 4,104 out-of-gamut colors), and `clampChroma` finds the sRGB chroma boundary that TASK-0021 caches.

A custom pipeline would mean writing and testing all of this ourselves, then deciding again in EPIC-0009 whether to keep it.

## Related

- TASK-0100 (EPIC-0020): swatch label contrast. 710 of 14,544 swatches miss WCAG AA, and the fix needs a decision on the `#1d1d1d` dark text color.
- EPIC-0006: builds OKLCH generation on culori.
- EPIC-0009: removes chroma.js once nothing depends on it.
```

```markdown
# TASK-0136: Parse target input with culori and gamut-map it

`parseTargetColor()` (`app/src/lib/colors.ts:25`) parses through chroma.js, which falls short of CSS Color 4 in three ways:

- **Rejected syntax:** `turn`, `rad` and `grad` hue units (`hsl(0.5turn …)`), comma-syntax `hsla()` with `deg`, `hwb()`, and `color(srgb …)` / `color(display-p3 …)` all fail to parse.
- **Rounding:** chroma.js rounds `hsl()` input to 8-bit RGB, which is why the `HSL_TOKENS` regex workaround exists. culori keeps typed values as given.
- **Clipping:** out-of-sRGB input is clipped per channel, which moves hue. `lch(50% 130 250)` clips to OKLCH hue 250.7, 56° from the input's 194.2. CSS Color 4 gamut mapping keeps it at 194.6.

Format detection is ours: `lch()`, `lab()` and `oklab()` input is detected as format "named", so the target row echoes it back as hex.

## Acceptance

- `parseTargetColor()` parses with culori's `parse`, and the `HSL_TOKENS` workaround is gone.
- Out-of-sRGB input goes through `toGamut("rgb", "oklch")` before hue and saturation are read.
- The format comes from culori's parsed mode. Decide which formats the target row echoes back; the rest fall back to hex explicitly.
- Existing `colors.test.ts` cases still pass (their vectors are in sRGB). New cases cover the syntax above, P3 input and `lch(50% 130 250)`.

## Source

- Color-accuracy review of EPIC-0009, 2026-11-04. Measured against colorjs.io 0.7.1, the CSS Color 4 reference implementation.
```

```markdown
# EPIC-0009: Migrate from chroma.js to culori

Make [culori](https://github.com/Evercoder/culori) the only color library and remove chroma.js. culori arrives with EPIC-0022 (TASK-0020), which also moves every chroma.js call whose output changes. This epic swaps the rest and removes the dependency. See EPIC-0022, "Why culori", for the measurements.

Swapping libraries doesn't change today's palettes: HSL→hex is identical for 266,375 of 266,640 inputs, and the other 265 are exact .5 channel ties.

## chroma.js call sites (2026-11-04)

- `lib/colors.ts`: label contrast (`getContrastColor`), target-color parsing and formatting (TASK-0134 and TASK-0136 move parsing and the `oklch()` formatter first)
- `lib/export.ts`: export conversions (TASK-0134 and TASK-0135 move `oklch()` and `lch()` first)
- `lib/palette.ts`: HSL generation, replaced by EPIC-0006 (TASK-0024)
- `components/TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`: target preview canvas
- `components/ChartTabs/ChartTabs.tsx`: unadjusted Compare strip
- `components/AboutButton/AboutButton.tsx`: educational strips, rewritten by EPIC-0008

## Scope

- Replace `chroma.contrast()` with culori's `wcagContrast`. Results match: both are within 0.001 of the reference.
- Replace the remaining `chroma.hsl()` and `chroma(hex)` calls: hex and rgb in `formatTargetColor()`, the rgb and GPL exports, `TargetSwatch.tsx`, `ChartTabs.tsx` and, after EPIC-0008, `AboutButton.tsx`.
- Remove `chroma-js` and `@types/chroma-js` from `app/package.json`.

## Blocked by

- TASK-0020 (EPIC-0022) adds culori. The contrast swap can move as soon as it lands.
- EPIC-0022 before removing chroma.js: it moves parsing and the `oklch()` and `lch()` conversions.
- EPIC-0006 before removing chroma.js: `palette.ts` generates with it until TASK-0024.
- EPIC-0008 for `AboutButton.tsx`: avoid migrating calls the rewrite replaces.

## Reference

- culori repo: https://github.com/Evercoder/culori
- EPIC-0022, "Why culori": accuracy measurements against colorjs.io, the CSS Color 4 reference implementation (2026-11-04)
- Q7 answer in NOTE-0006 analysis *(superseded 2026-11-04)*: "A wholesale switch to culori is a future cleanup task, not a migration blocker"
```

```text
# EPIC-0016: About dialog narrative refresh

The About dialog currently frames Chroma Curve solely as a fix for a perceptual problem — fixed/static saturation produces uneven chroma, and the parabolic curve corrects it. That framing is accurate but incomplete:

1. It primes users to interpret the tool as **corrective only**, when the same curve mechanism enables genuinely creative palette shapes (vivid mids, muted mids, asymmetric scales).
2. The example labels ("Fixed low saturation," "Fixed high saturation") use *fixed* in the sense of "constant," but in a context all about correcting problems, *fixed* reads ambiguously as "corrected." This is exactly the wrong read.

## Goals

- Disambiguate the "fixed saturation" labels so the comparison strips clearly mean "constant/static," not "corrected."
- Extend the narrative beyond problem-solving to include the creative applications of the curve — both the default smoothing direction and (eventually) the inverted boost direction (TASK-0080).
- Keep the existing "show the math" rigor — this is a content layer on top, not a replacement.

## Out of scope

- The OKLCH rewrite (EPIC-0008 covers reframing for the post-migration mental model).
- Visual redesign of the dialog itself — copy and structure only.

## Tasks

- TASK-0084 — Disambiguate "fixed saturation" labels
- TASK-0085 — Add creative applications section

## Related
```
